rules.element: change and effective dates, changed content
rules.statement: When the policy changes, continuously publish the change and effective dates and the changed content.

Publish earlier versions together with the current one so each version's application period can be checked (web: list of periods linking to each version; offline: record the history and keep earlier versions for viewing or provision on request).
Announce changes by easily noticed means such as a notice board post or pop-up.
For changes with significant impact on rights (e.g. items processed, purposes), give a separate before/after comparison (대조표 or similar) before or at the time of revision.

Frequently changing, low-impact items (e.g. lists of processors or sub-processors for the same task) may be announced in batches over a reasonable period (e.g. 4 weeks); each list entry must still show the start and end of the outsourcing.

check.expr: if(notice.batched) every(notice.rows, r => r.start && (r.end || r.ongoing)) && notice.windowDays <= 28

changes2026.summary: 2026.4 improved the change-notice method (revision history L27-30). The guideline does not itemize which sub-rules are new; new2026 flags mark the change-notice rules as a group.
items: version list with application periods and links
before/after comparison table for rights-affecting changes, before or at revision
batched notice for minor list changes over a reasonable window (example 4 weeks) with start/end dates
notice via board or pop-up recommended

batched: table: before | after | task | effective date

goodPatterns: Clause 1: this policy applies from <date>. Clause 2: earlier versions listed as '<from> ~ <to> 적용' each linked.

commonDefects.defect: Earlier versions not viewable or listed without application periods.
Purpose or item changes announced without a comparison table, or only after taking effect.
Batched processor-change notice lacks start/end dates.

needsVerification.note: R-S24-004 'must' reflects the guideline wording (하여야 함) but no statute is cited for the comparison table; legal review to confirm severity for the rubric.
